entries.name: AI Engineer Coach
entries.use_for: See how you use AI coding assistants and get tips from local session logs.
entries.why: Reads local logs from many harnesses and checks them against 45 anti-pattern rules.
entries.summary: A VS Code extension and GitHub Copilot canvas that reads local AI session logs. It shows practice scores, trends, anti-patterns, generated code volume and repeated prompts that could become skills. No data leaves your machine.
entries.best_for: Developers or teams who want to improve how they use coding agents.
entries.not_for: Built from source as a VSIX per the README. It analyzes usage and does not help build products.

entries.name: CC GUI
entries.use_for: Use Claude Code and Codex from a visual chat panel inside JetBrains IDEs.
entries.why: Adds @file context, image input, conversation rewind, skills slash commands and MCP support.
entries.summary: An IntelliJ IDEA plugin that wraps Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and other AI coding CLIs in a graphical interface. It has an agent system, slash commands and MCP server support.
entries.best_for: JetBrains users who want a GUI instead of the terminal for coding agents.
entries.not_for: Renamed from Claude Code GUI over trademark concerns and under active change. macOS may scroll slowly unless GPU acceleration is disabled.

entries.name: CC Workflow Studio
entries.use_for: Design AI agent workflows on a visual canvas and export them as Markdown your agent can run.
entries.why: One workflow.json drives a VS Code editor, a CLI and an MCP server.
entries.summary: A VS Code extension with a drag-and-drop canvas for multi-agent workflows with sub-agents, skills and MCP tools. The same file works with the ccwf CLI (render, validate, export, run) and an MCP server.
entries.best_for: Designing and sharing Claude Code agent workflows visually instead of writing prompts by hand.
entries.not_for: Anyone who does not use VS Code or Claude Code style agents. Usage examples are marked as coming soon, and the licence is not clearly stated.

entries.name: Chrome Extensions Samples
entries.use_for: Official Manifest V3 sample extensions for every Chrome extension API
entries.why: Canonical reference code from the Chrome team for each extension API
entries.summary: Official Chrome team repository of sample extensions. Contains api-samples (one API each) and functional-samples (multi-API, full-featured extensions), plus archived MV2 and deprecated Chrome Apps material.
entries.best_for: Learning how to use specific Chrome extension APIs with Manifest V3 reference code.
entries.not_for: A build framework or boilerplate; these are standalone samples, not tooling. Chrome Apps content is deprecated.

entries.name: Claudian
entries.use_for: Use Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents inside an Obsidian vault.
entries.why: The vault becomes the agent's working directory, with inline edit, @mentions and MCP support.
entries.summary: Claudian is an Obsidian plugin that embeds AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, OpenCode, Pi, DeepSeek Harness) in your vault. Agents can read, write, edit, search and run commands there. It adds inline edit with diff preview, slash commands, skills, @mentions and MCP servers.
entries.best_for: Obsidian users who want an agent to work directly on their notes.
entries.not_for: Mobile or non-Obsidian use. It is desktop only and needs at least one agent harness plus a subscription or API provider.

entries.name: CRXJS Vite plugin
entries.use_for: Vite plugin to build Chrome extensions with HMR, using manifest.json as the entry
entries.why: Lightweight alternative to WXT/Plasmo when you just want Vite plus a manifest
entries.summary: Vite plugin for building Chrome (and cross-browser) extensions using manifest.json as the entry point. Provides HMR including for content scripts, static asset imports, automatic web_accessible_resources and full use of Vite plugins; scaffold with npm create crxjs.
entries.best_for: Teams who want plain Vite plus a manifest with HMR for Manifest V3 extensions.
entries.not_for: Opinionated frameworks with built-in messaging, storage and publishing (WXT, Plasmo). MV2 support lives in a separate rollup-plugin.

entries.name: DSH Better Sidebar
entries.use_for: Add a file, Git, terminal and side-chat workbench to DSH and let other plugins add pages.
entries.why: Exposes a sidebar service so third-party plugins can register new pages.
entries.summary: A plugin for DSH that adds a right sidebar and bottom panel. It includes a file tree and editor, Git source control with a read-only commit graph, terminals, side chat threads and subagent task views.
entries.best_for: DSH users who want a richer workbench, or plugin authors who want sidebar hooks.
entries.not_for: Only useful with the DSH host app, which the README does not describe. Side chat is marked beta.

entries.name: Extension.js
entries.use_for: Scaffold, develop and build cross-browser extensions with zero config.
entries.why: Framework-agnostic extension tooling with many templates; MIT.
entries.summary: Zero-config tooling to scaffold, develop and build cross-browser extensions. Aims to fix browser-specific quirks and missing content-script hot reload, with many templates and framework-agnostic setup.
entries.best_for: Starting cross-browser extensions quickly with templates and a ready dev/build pipeline.
entries.not_for: Projects tied to Vite plugin ecosystems or needing the larger communities around WXT/Plasmo; check maturity before betting on it.

entries.name: IntelliJ Platform Plugin Template
entries.use_for: Template repository for creating plugins for IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs
entries.why: Official JetBrains starter with Gradle setup, CI and publishing preconfigured
entries.summary: Official JetBrains template repository for starting IntelliJ Platform plugins. Pre-configures the Gradle project scaffold, CI, publishing and links to documentation.
entries.best_for: Starting a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA or other JetBrains IDEs with recommended structure, CI and publishing already set.
entries.not_for: Non-JetBrains editors, or ones who want scaffolding via a CLI generator; this is a GitHub template repo for Kotlin/Java plugin projects.

entries.name: llm-for-zotero
entries.use_for: Chat with, summarize and compare papers inside Zotero, with an agent mode that uses your library.
entries.why: Works with API providers, local OpenAI-compatible models, Codex App Server and Claude Code, with custom skills.
entries.summary: A Zotero plugin that adds an LLM assistant to the reader and library. It can answer questions, inspect figures, compare papers and save notes as Zotero or Markdown files. An agent mode has built-in skills and web search.
entries.best_for: Researchers who want LLM help inside Zotero, or developers learning how to build a Zotero plugin with an agent.
entries.not_for: Only works inside Zotero. The Claude Code mode is experimental and lacks native Zotero API operations. AGPL-3.0 licensed.

entries.name: Obsidian API
entries.use_for: Official TypeScript API definitions for building Obsidian plugins
entries.why: The typed API every Obsidian plugin depends on, with docs in the declarations
entries.summary: Official TypeScript type definitions for the Obsidian plugin API, with documentation in TSDoc comments. Describes plugin structure including manifest.json fields and main.js.
entries.best_for: Writing typed Obsidian plugins; every plugin depends on it for the API surface.
entries.not_for: A starter project (use obsidian-sample-plugin) or non-Obsidian note apps; it contains only type declarations, not implementation.

entries.name: Obsidian Sample Plugin
entries.use_for: Start an Obsidian community plugin with the official build setup.
entries.why: Official Obsidian template used by most community plugins.
entries.summary: Official template for Obsidian community plugins in TypeScript. Demonstrates a ribbon icon, a command opening a modal, a settings tab, a global click event and a registered interval.
entries.best_for: Starting a new Obsidian community plugin with the standard build and structure.
entries.not_for: Any non-Obsidian target; it is a minimal demo to adapt, not a framework or feature-rich scaffold.

entries.name: Plasmo
entries.use_for: Build browser extensions with React and TypeScript using a batteries-included framework.
entries.why: Popular extension framework with built-in messaging, storage and store publishing.
entries.summary: Framework for building browser extensions with React and TypeScript, described as batteries-included with built-in messaging, storage and store publishing. No README content was provided; details rely on general knowledge.
entries.best_for: React/TypeScript browser extensions where you want integrated messaging, storage and automated store submission.
entries.not_for: Maintenance-sensitive projects: check current activity, as WXT is often considered the more actively developed alternative. Opinionated and framework-driven.

entries.name: Raycast Extensions
entries.use_for: Build and publish Raycast extensions, using thousands of existing ones as references.
entries.why: Official repo for Raycast Store extensions with templates and contribution workflow.
entries.summary: Monorepo of all extensions in the Raycast Store, plus documentation and examples for extending Raycast using React and the Raycast API. Contribution and acceptable-use guidelines apply when submitting.
entries.best_for: Writing and publishing a Raycast extension, using existing store extensions as references.
entries.not_for: Anything outside Raycast (macOS/Windows launcher); not a general framework. Publishing requires following store guidelines and review.

entries.name: vite-plugin-monkey
entries.use_for: Vite plugin for building Tampermonkey, Violentmonkey and Greasemonkey userscripts
entries.why: Brings Vite dev server, HMR and frameworks to userscript development
entries.summary: Vite plugin for building userscripts for Tampermonkey, Violentmonkey, Greasemonkey and ScriptCat. Injects metadata, auto-configures @grant from used GM APIs, supports @require/@resource externals, ESM GM imports with types, TypeScript and top-level await.
entries.best_for: Userscript projects wanting Vite, TypeScript and frameworks with dev-server workflow.
entries.not_for: Full browser extensions with manifests (use WXT/CRXJS) or tiny one-file scripts that do not need a build step.

entries.name: VS Code Extension Samples
entries.use_for: Start a VS Code extension from official samples covering most extension APIs.
entries.why: Microsoft's official reference samples for the VS Code extension API.
entries.summary: Microsoft's official collection of self-contained sample extensions, each demonstrating one VS Code API or contribution point with explanation, usage gif and code. Run any sample with F5 after npm install.
entries.best_for: Learning how to implement specific VS Code extension features by example.
entries.not_for: A project scaffold or build tool (use yo code); samples are reference code to copy from, not a library.

entries.name: vsce
entries.use_for: Package and publish VS Code extensions to the Marketplace
entries.why: Official tool for packaging .vsix files and publishing extensions
entries.summary: Official command-line tool (@vscode/vsce) for packaging VS Code extensions into .vsix files and publishing them to the Marketplace. Also exposes a small library API. Requires Node 22+.
entries.best_for: Packaging and publishing VS Code extensions from CLI or CI.
entries.not_for: Writing extensions or publishing to the Open VSX registry (use ovsx). It is only the packaging and publish step.

entries.name: web-ext
entries.use_for: CLI to run, lint, package and sign browser extensions
entries.why: Official Mozilla tool for developing and publishing Firefox (and Chromium) extensions
entries.summary: Mozilla's command-line tool to run, lint, build and sign WebExtensions. Runs extensions in Firefox (including Firefox for Android via adb) and has a programmatic API.
entries.best_for: Developing, testing and publishing Firefox extensions; auto-reload and linting for WebExtensions.
entries.not_for: A full build/bundling framework; it does not bundle your code. Focused on Firefox, with Chromium support secondary.

entries.name: WXT
entries.use_for: Build cross-browser web extensions with Vite, HMR and file-based entrypoints.
entries.why: Modern, fast-growing extension framework with excellent DX; MIT.
entries.summary: Next-gen web extension framework, described as Nuxt for web extensions. Built on Vite with HMR, file-based entrypoints, auto-imports, TypeScript, a module system, bundle analysis and automated publishing; supports all browsers, MV2 and MV3, and any UI framework.
entries.best_for: New cross-browser extensions with React, Vue or Svelte that want a modern dev experience and automated publishing.
entries.not_for: Tiny scripts or userscripts, or teams wanting just a Vite plugin with minimal conventions (CRXJS). Adds framework conventions to learn.

entries.name: Yo Code
entries.use_for: Scaffold new VS Code extensions, themes, language support and more
entries.why: Official Microsoft generator used in the VS Code extension docs
entries.summary: Yeoman generator (yo code) that scaffolds VS Code extensions, themes, language support and more. Creates a base folder structure, package.json, assets and launch.json for debugging.
entries.best_for: Starting a new VS Code extension or theme with the official templates.
entries.not_for: Ongoing build or packaging needs, or non-VS Code editors; it is a one-time scaffold that depends on Yeoman.
